title: Applications of Spin-Dependent Generalized Squeezing in Hybrid Spin-Oscillator Quantum Processors
authors: Kai Shinbrough, Donovan J. Webb, Iver R. Øvergaard, Oana Băzăvan, Sebastian Saner, Christopher J. Ballance, Raghavendra Srinivas
abstract: Generalized squeezing interactions are foundational to quantum optics, and have recently come under experimental control in hybrid spin-oscillator quantum processors [O. Băzăvan, et al., Nat. Phys. 22, 757 (2026); S. Saner, et al., Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049 (2026)]. These interactions open the door for new applications in the processing of discrete- and continuous-variable quantum information, four of which we propose and investigate in this work: geometric phase gates mediated by spin-dependent generalized squeezing acting on two spins and a common oscillator; genuine N-body spin interactions mediated by individually addressed spin-dependent generalized squeezing; oscillator thermometry via spin readout; and the preparation of high-fidelity quantum states of the oscillator via spin-dependent generalized squeezing and mid-circuit measurement. A unifying feature of these applications is the geometric phase induced by generalized squeezing interactions, which is nonlinear in the Fock occupation of the oscillator and the interaction order of the generalized squeezing. This work provides a foundation for fast, high-fidelity discrete- and continuous-variable quantum computation and sensing in the hybrid spin-oscillator platform via generalized squeezing.
summary: This paper details how generalized squeezing interactions can be harnessed to realize several key applications in hybrid spin-oscillator quantum processors. The research focuses on developing fast and high-fidelity methods for both discrete and continuous variable quantum computation and sensing. By leveraging the geometric phase inherent in these interactions, it establishes a robust theoretical framework for next-generation quantum hardware.
main_problem: The work proposes four novel applications for utilizing spin-dependent generalized squeezing interactions to achieve fast, high-fidelity quantum computation and sensing.
main_result: These applications demonstrate that the geometric phase induced by generalized squeezing provides a foundation for advanced discrete- and continuous-variable quantum processing in hybrid platforms.
method: The analysis involves deriving time evolution using the Magnus expansion applied to Hamiltonians describing spin-oscillator coupling, leading to engineered gates and interactions.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid spin-oscillator platform, modeled by an interaction Hamiltonian involving collective spin operators ($\hat{J}_{	heta,\phi}$) and bosonic ladder operators ($\hat{a}, \hat{a}^\dagger$).
key_observables: Gate fidelity, gate speedup ($S(k)$), Wigner function trajectories, and the effective Rabi frequency for N-body interactions.
important_parameters: The interaction order $k$ of the generalized squeezing, the initial Fock state occupation ($n_i$), and detunings ($\delta_j$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: Calculations rely on truncating the Magnus expansion (e.g., to second order), and the set of applications discussed is noted as non-exhaustive.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates Wigner function trajectories comparing $k=1$ (displacement) and $k=2$ (squeezing) gates, alongside plots showing gate speedup versus initial Fock state occupation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates four applications: geometric phase gates for two spins/one oscillator; genuine N-body spin interactions; oscillator thermometry via spin readout; and high-fidelity quantum state preparation of the oscillator.
why_interesting: It directly addresses advanced control techniques (generalized squeezing) in hybrid systems, providing concrete protocols for implementing complex quantum gates beyond standard pairwise interactions.
